findings.finding: The r7 execution_plan_template step_3 ('re-run ALL of step_0_recheck against the ORIGINAL path' after hold) is unimplementable as written: after staging+commit, the original path no longer exists, and gate1 on it shows the quarantine commit itself (observed: gate1-post pushed.txt lines=1, docs/pushed-deep.txt lines=1). A pushed receipt cannot survive its own staging commit.

Second-check algorithm must be receipt-class-split (validated): pushed = pre-stage receipt evidence (of record) + post-hold sha256 identity + no-resurrection; stale = real tool re-run on the quarantined copy (sweep excludes quarantine, so it re-verifies) + identity.
evidence: step4-negatives.txt (stale copy SAFE, pushed copy NOT-SAFE on same probe)

findings.finding: This seat's own staging commit used 'git add -A' and silently committed the secret-shaped .env and the too-young launch-new.json alongside the 4 staged paths (git show --stat 9f976d1: 6 files incl. .env | 1 +). Runbook rule: quarantine staging commits must be path-scoped (git mv stages itself; plain-mv'd files added by explicit path). Remediated and proven in repoA2 (commit feb73f2: exactly 2 paths; .env/launch-new.json/notes-draft.md remain untracked).
--stale-days 0 turns a brand-new scratch file into SAFE(stale) (mtime-age-days=0 passes when threshold is 0). Runbook must pin --stale-days 1 or the tool default; 0 is a false-SAFE enabler.

Receipt-break-during-hold is caught: an injection commit adding a live reference to notes-draft.md flipped the quarantined copy from SAFE(stale refs=0) to NOT-SAFE(stale=live-refs=1); its deletion was aborted and the copy held in quarantine.

gate2 as templated ('porcelain must print nothing') is unsatisfiable for untracked scratch candidates (their natural state is '??'), yet SKILL.md's flow explicitly supports plain mv for untracked. For untracked stale candidates gate2 must read: porcelain over the path may show ONLY '??' — never M/A (a modified tracked file is live work). Observed: gate2 launch-old.json <<?? launch-old.json>> while its stale receipt was legitimately establishable.

No-remote control fail-closed: repoB/b.txt -> NOT-SAFE(pushed-unverifiable, no-default-ref). Shared-remote fixture footgun: repoA2's push to the same bare remote was rejected non-fast-forward; fixture remotes must be per-repo (isolated remote2.git used).

runbook_corrections.corrected: Second check is receipt-class-split. PUSHED: retained pre-stage receipt evidence (step_0_recheck output, of record) + post-hold sha256(quarantined copy)==pre-stage hash + original path not resurrected. Never re-run the pushed receipt post-staging — the staging commit itself destroys it (observed NOT-SAFE(unpushed-commits-touching intro=<quarantine-commit>) on quarantined pushed copies in both repoA and repoA2). STALE: bash tools/souji-verify.sh --json <quarantined copy> must still print SAFE(stale) — the sweep excludes .ufo-quarantine so this re-run is meaningful — plus the same identity check.

Quarantine staging commits MUST be path-scoped: git mv stages itself; for plain-mv'd untracked files use git add -- .ufo-quarantine/<date>/<name>. Never git add -A — observed to sweep in .env (secret-shaped) and an unapproved candidate into commit 9f976d1; repoA2 commit feb73f2 proves the scoped form commits exactly the staged paths.
Runbook pins --stale-days 1 (or tool default) in every stale receipt invocation; --stale-days 0 marks brand-new scratch SAFE(stale) (observed: mtime-age-days=0 file SAFE at threshold 0).

Post-hold deletions from quarantine are git rm -q -- <paths> + a commit naming receipt class, hold elapsed, and second-check evidence; an abort case stays in quarantine un-deleted and is recorded (observed: notes-draft.md held, live-refs=1).
